🇲🇽🇨🇱 <u>KAST'S CARABINEROS GAS THE STUDENTS — CHILE'S ULTRA-RIGHT REPRISES THE PINOCHET PLAYBOOK</u>

Yesterday's Confech national strike ended with carabineros firing water cannons and tear gas at students in Plaza Baquedano and along the Alameda. They were protesting Kast's new repressive law: police searches of student backpacks, plus a five-year ban from free university for any kid who "commits a crime in the classroom."

Same week he's pushing a bill to cut corporate income tax from 27% to 23%. The classic ledger: more riot police on poor kids, lower taxes on capital. This is exactly what the Mexican ultraderecha is rooting for at home — and what they had us under for thirty years before Morena.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>HUACHICOL GAS TANKERS EXPLODE IN TEPEACA — PUEBLA IS THE NATIONAL EPICENTER</u>

Four "huachigas" tankers detonated at 9:53 AM today in San Juan Negrete, Tepeaca — 2,000 evacuated including 1,753 schoolchildren and the General Hospital. A smoke column over 15 meters high was visible across the municipality; three injured.

Tepeaca alone registered 44 clandestine LP gas taps in Q1 2026 — 28% of all of Puebla's 157 — and Puebla state's illegal-tap count jumped 35.34% year-over-year. The fire is exposing the scale of a private theft network built under the old PAN-PRI regime. Networks two decades in the making don't dismantle quietly.

🇲🇽🌎 "There's a relationship of respect. I have my reservations about it being President Trump." On Trump's public praise of her administration and US Homeland Security Secretary Mullin telling Congress that Sheinbaum's government has surpassed cooperation of any recent Mexican administration. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo She accepts the recognition of the Mexican State but doesn't normalize the person or the project. The same week she's denouncing the US far-right campaign against Mexico, she keeps the diplomatic channel open without flattering it. A line, not a hug.

🇲🇽⚽ "Not just the matches — and then it leaves. Use the World Cup to build the country." Sheinbaum's frame for the Mundial Social: 1,200 new federal football fields, 1.13 million kids in the school tournament across 28,621 schools, 43% girls' participation, programs for seniors and people with Down syndrome. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo 7 days from kickoff. The bet is that the kids playing on those new pitches become the pipeline for the next generation of professionals. World Cup as social infrastructure, not as a neoliberal storefront.

🇲🇽⚽ Iran's national team arrives in Tijuana tomorrow — because the US wouldn't let them stay. "Iran's national team arrives tomorrow in Tijuana, because they are going to train there due to some situations they have with the United States." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Iran plays its three group-stage matches in the US — against New Zealand, Belgium and Egypt — but Washington refused to let the delegation sleep on US soil. Asked if Mexico could host them, the answer was: yes, no problem. Their base will be the Xolos training center on the Tijuana border.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico signs national tomato agreement to cut out intermediaries. "What we are seeking is to reduce those intermediaries. To have a direct agreement between the producer and whoever sells the tomato — central market, supermarket, tianguis, or any other form of commercialization." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Producers from 18 states, central wholesale markets, tianguis and supermarket chains signed on. Targets the price spike that pushed tomato to 80 pesos/kilo this season — driven by a plague in Sinaloa and Florida plus middlemen. National market gets priority over export.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum names the calendar behind the US campaign against Mexico. "A very strong campaign has been unleashed — because of their November 2026 elections they want to use Mexico in their rhetoric, and to ally with the Mexican far-right for the 2027 election." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Two electoral cycles, one operation: US midterms in November 2026, Mexican midterms in 2027. Mexico used as a foreign-policy prop for US domestic politics, and as fuel for the local opposition heading into the next vote. The president is naming the timeline out loud.
